What photos to send — a 60-second guide

You do not need to shoot anything new. Send the photos you already have. This tells you which ones, and what to add if something is missing.

The short version

  • 4 photos minimum. 8–14 is the sweet spot.
  • Landscape, not portrait. Turn the phone sideways.
  • Originals, straight off the camera or phone. Do not crop, filter or brighten them. We do not edit your photos either — that is deliberate, and it is what keeps the finished video compliant.
  • Name each file after the room: kitchen.jpg, master-bedroom.jpg. If you number them (01_, 02_) we will keep that exact order.

The three we cannot make a tour without

  1. The front of the house — Stand on the walkway square to the front of the house. Keep the camera level — do not tilt up.
  2. The main living room — Stand in the doorway you enter by, with the far side of the room in frame.
  3. The kitchen — Stand where you can see the island or main counter and the way through to the next room.

Without these the video still renders, but it reads as incomplete to a buyer, and we will tell you so before we charge you for it.

Then add as many of these as you have

Order does not matter — we sequence them the way a buyer walks the house.

Room Name the file
The street / driveway approach street

The entry or front hallway entry
The main living room living required

The office or study office

Any other bathroom bathroom never used as the cover frame
The laundry / utility room laundry never used as the cover frame
The lower level basement

The patio, deck or porch patio

The view (water, mountains, skyline) view
An aerial / drone shot, if you have one aerial

Two rules that matter more than they look

1. The aerial rule. If you send an aerial, it must be shot over the same side of the house as the outdoor photo before it, and the filename must say which side (rear-aerial.jpg).

Here is why. The video moves the camera between your photos. If the last ground photo looks at the back of the house and the aerial is framed over the front, there is no path a real drone could fly between them — so the video has to cross the building, and it comes out looking like a different house. We learned this the hard way on our own test.

2. Do not jump from the front of the house to the back with nothing in between. Send a side view, or an aerial, as the bridge.

What makes a photo unusable

  • Portrait orientation
  • Heavily filtered, HDR-crunched or brightened
  • A room shot so tight there is no doorway or opening visible
  • People or pets in frame
  • Screenshots of photos, or photos re-saved from a text message

What happens next

Send the folder. We check it, tell you within a couple of hours if anything is missing, and deliver the video the next day.
